findings.finding: The AST regression test can pass vacuously and covers only a fixed set of modules. It asserts that every `subprocess.run`/`runner.run` call with `text=True` also passes `encoding="utf-8"`. It does not assert that at least one such call is found per module. So a module that uses `check_output`, `Popen`, `universal_newlines=True`, or a `text` kwarg passed through `**kwargs` would pass trivially. The test is also hardcoded to five modules, while the lint rule is explicitly rejected because it would miss this class. A future sixth CLI consumer would regress silently.
findings.location: Testing, bullet 3 (AST check of the five CLI-consumer modules)
scenarios: One of the five modules calls through a helper or uses `universal_newlines=True`. The test finds zero matching calls and passes both before and after the fix.

findings.finding: Reconfiguring the CLI's stdout/stderr to UTF-8 changes what bytes rebar emits on Windows. Before the fix, child and parent both used cp1252, so non-ASCII characters that cp1252 can encode (e.g. em dash) made the round trip intact. After the fix, any parent that captures rebar output with `text=True` and no `encoding` decodes UTF-8 bytes as cp1252. Most non-ASCII characters then come out garbled (e.g. '—' becomes 'â€”'). Bytes that cp1252 leaves undefined raise UnicodeDecodeError: 0x9d, the last byte of '”' in UTF-8, is one of them. The plan updates only five product consumers and the test modules already in text-encoding.args. Many other tests launch `[sys.executable, "-m", "rebar", ...]` and capture its output; those that pass today on Windows can start failing, which puts the `sweep (windows)` success acceptance criterion at risk.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the sequencing: run `gh workflow run test.yml --ref <branch>` with the lines removed before merge (or define the post-merge re-add procedure for any removed test that still fails), and record that run id.
evidence: "Remove each fixed line from `text-encoding.args`"
"Windows: `gh workflow run test.yml --ref main` after merge."
AC: "Every line removed from `text-encoding.args` names a test that passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix"
findings.finding: The acceptance criteria and the steps are mis-sequenced. The plan removes 'each fixed line' from text-encoding.args in the change itself. Yet the AC requires every removed line to name a test that passed in a `sweep (windows)` run on main after the fix, and Testing schedules that run only after merge. While a line is still deselected, the test cannot run on Windows. So the decision about which lines are 'fixed' must be made before any Windows evidence exists. Nothing says what happens if a removed test then fails post-merge.
findings.location: Approach (last paragraph) vs Testing ('Windows: gh workflow run test.yml --ref main after merge') vs AC 3/4
scenarios: A removed test still fails on Windows for an unanticipated reason (e.g. a git subprocess decoded as cp1252). The post-merge sweep fails, and AC 4 cannot be met without an unplanned follow-up.
findings.suggested_fix: Before merge, dispatch the sweep on the PR branch with all 133 lines removed. Re-add (with a reason) any line whose test still fails, then confirm on main after merge.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default: the hook test copies or points the hook at a `tmp_path` project root (seeding the cp1252 stale `_build_info.py` there) and never writes into the repo's `src/rebar`.
evidence: "runs the hatch hook's `initialize` in a subprocess ... and asserts the generated file decodes as UTF-8; edge: a cp1252 stale `_build_info.py` yields no baked SHA"
findings.finding: The hatch-hook regression test runs the hook's `initialize` in a subprocess, but the plan does not say which root it writes to. Run against the repo, it would overwrite the developer's real `src/rebar/_build_info.py`, and other tests scan that file. The stale-file edge case needs a seeded cp1252 file, which also implies an isolated tree.
findings.location: Testing, bullet 1 (hatch hook initialize subprocess test)
scenarios: The test rewrites `src/rebar/_build_info.py` in the working tree. A test-order dependency appears with tree scans, or a stale cp1252 fixture leaks into the checkout.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the newline rule for the other text-mode write sites: add `newline="\n"` wherever the file is canonical, hashed or byte-compared (list which), or record that CRLF is acceptable for the rest.
evidence: "`bindings.json` written with CRLF (product)"
"`binding_repository.py:76`: add `newline=\"\n\"`."
"The 17 other locale-default text calls ... get `encoding=\"utf-8\"`" (no newline decision)
findings.finding: Root cause 3 identifies CRLF translation on Windows text-mode writes as a defect class, but `newline="\n"` is added only to `binding_repository.py`. Several of the 17 newly-UTF-8 sites appear to be writes, judging by their names (e.g. `reducer/marker.py:24,53`, `reconciler/sync_logger.py:32`, `apply_planning.py`, `pass_io.py`). The plan does not say whether those also need `newline="\n"` or whether CRLF is acceptable for them.
findings.location: Approach (`binding_repository.py:76` newline bullet vs the 17-site PLW1514 bullet); Context root cause 3
scenarios: A marker or canonical JSON file written via one of those sites is compared byte-wise or hashed across hosts. It differs on Windows because of CRLF, which is the same failure mode as bindings.json.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the disposition of the stale-file arm and of the composed 'no baked SHA + no git' path, and preserve the ASCII SHA from a non-UTF-8 stale file rather than discarding it.
evidence: "`_read_existing_commit` also treats `UnicodeDecodeError` as \"no baked SHA\""
"edge: a cp1252 stale `_build_info.py` yields no baked SHA instead of raising"
No statement covers the outcome when both the baked-SHA read and the git lookup fail.
findings.finding: The new degrade arm in `_read_existing_commit` treats UnicodeDecodeError as 'no baked SHA'. This discards a recoverable value: the SHA in a stale cp1252 `_build_info.py` is pure ASCII, and only the docstring em dash is undecodable. The plan does not state what the hook surfaces when that arm fires and git is also unavailable. In that case, which is the scenario the baked SHA exists for (e.g. building from an sdist or archive without .git), provenance silently degrades to absent or unknown.
findings.location: Approach — hatch_build.py bullet ('`_read_existing_commit` also treats `UnicodeDecodeError` as "no baked SHA"')
scenarios: A source tree previously built on Windows (cp1252 `_build_info.py`) is rebuilt without .git; the valid baked SHA is thrown away and the wheel ships with no commit provenance.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the stale file as bytes, or with `errors="replace"`, and extract the ASCII SHA. Treat it as 'no baked SHA' only when no SHA pattern matches. Document what the hook writes when neither the baked SHA nor git is available.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate in-process callers of `_cli.main` and either confine the reconfigure to the console-script/`__main__` entry or restore the original encoding on exit.
evidence: "when `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` is an `io.TextIOWrapper` whose encoding is not UTF-8, `reconfigure(encoding=\"utf-8\")`"
"a no-op on Linux/macOS and under pytest capture" — no statement about in-process embedders or restoration.
findings.finding: Reconfiguring `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` inside `main` is a process-global mutation with no restore. The plan claims it is a no-op under pytest capture, but it does not enumerate in-process callers of `main` (library facades, the MCP server, tests run with `-s`). Nor does it state whether those callers' streams may be changed for the rest of the process.
findings.location: Approach — `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` `main` (`:306`) bullet
scenarios: A host process (or a pytest run with `-s` on a Windows CI pipe) calls `main()` in-process; its stdout encoding is permanently switched, changing the bytes of all its later output.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the reconfigure into the `__main__`/console-script entry wrapper, so that `main()` called as a library function does not mutate the host's streams.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-derive the CLI-output consumer list with Serena `find_referencing_symbols` on `rebar._engine.in_process_cli` and `rebar.reconciler.invariants._default_ticket_cli`, and also do a string search (`in_process_cli`, `"rebar"` argv constants), then record the method on the ticket.
evidence: Plan: "Found with `git grep -n 'in_process_cli()\|"-m", "rebar"' -- src scripts`, plus the `ticket_cli` runner callers"

The grep pattern `"-m", "rebar"` needs a closing quote right after `rebar`, so it cannot match argv built from variables or from a `RUNNER = [sys.executable, "-m", "rebar"]` constant split across lines. `in_process_cli()` with parentheses misses references to the function that never call it (e.g. `Path(in_process_cli())` is caught, but `resolve=in_process_cli` would not be).
findings.finding: The plan builds its consumer list for `rebar._engine.in_process_cli` / the `ticket_cli` runner / `python -m rebar` subprocesses from a `git grep` text search, not from a symbol-reference lookup. Text search misses aliased imports (e.g. `from rebar._engine import in_process_cli as ...`), callables passed as values (`resolve_ticket_cli=_default_ticket_cli`), and argv lists assembled from variables. I could not find a missed site, so this finding is advisory and rests on the derivation method alone.
findings.location: Approach — 'Every product parent that captures the rebar CLI's output in text mode decodes it as UTF-8' bullet
scenarios: A future or aliased consumer of `in_process_cli` that passes the function as a value or under another name would not be found. It would keep decoding the newly-UTF-8 CLI stdout with cp1252 on Windows and produce mojibake or a parse failure, and the AST regression test would not catch it because it only scans the five named modules.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `find_referencing_symbols` on `in_process_cli` and `_default_ticket_cli`, plus a plain string search for `in_process_cli` and for argv lists containing "rebar" (including `monkeypatch.setattr(..., "in_process_cli", ...)` in tests). Confirm the five modules are the full set and say on the ticket that the list is symbol-graph-derived.
